subject: SLA phasing request for APAC region — uptime % and monthly credit proposal
messages:
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@cumulushealth.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: ops@cumulushealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA expectations for APAC deployment

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're excited to move forward with Redwood for our APAC rollout, but a couple of operational items came up in our internal review we need aligned before we sign:

1) Uptime target — our procurement team typically asks for a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment across the account. Because APAC traffic will initially be routed through shared pools, we want to understand if you can guarantee the same SLA regionally or if a phased commitment is possible.

2) Monthly service credits — if you do offer a phased uptime (e.g., lower guarantee for the first 90 days), we need the credit schedule spelled out. Our legal team generally expects a simple percentage-of-invoice credit tied to the downtime band.

Could you share an updated SLA template (redlines welcome) and a suggestion on how Redwood typically handles regional phasing? Also attaching our traffic snapshot for May so you can see expected volumes.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement window is tight.

Best,
Susan
Susan Lee
Head of Cloud Ops, Cumulus Health

Attachment: Cumulus_APAC_Traffic_Report_May2026.csv (CSV)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@cumulushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA expectations for APAC deployment

Hi Susan —

Thanks for the traffic file and the clear asks. High level answer up front: we can support a regional phasing approach for APAC to account for initial pooling/placement differences. Below is a proposal we use as a playbook and that we think maps well to Cumulus's needs. If you want, Ben (sales) and Laura (legal) can prepare a single redlined SLA doc.

Proposed phased SLA & credits (suggested):
- Phase 1 (first 90 days after go-live): regional uptime commitment = 99.90%
  - Monthly credit for downtime: 5% of that month's Redwood invoice for the affected region if uptime < 99.90% and >= 99.50%
  - If uptime < 99.50% then credit = 10% of that month's Redwood invoice for APAC services
- Phase 2 (day 91 onward): regional uptime commitment = 99.95%
  - Monthly credit tiers: 5% credit if uptime is 99.8–99.95%, 10% if 99.5–99.8%, 25% if < 99.5%
- Global failover: if service degrades across multiple regions due to Redwood fault, crediting reverts to account-level formula in the master SLA

Additional guardrails / clarifications:
- Maintenance windows agreed in advance are excluded from uptime calculations when notified >72 hours prior
- Root cause must be validated by Redwood to trigger crediting (standard evidence package provided)
- Credit cap: for Phase 1 we recommend a monthly credit cap of 25% of the APAC invoice; for Phase 2 the standard cap is 50% (we can discuss)

I'll attach a draft SLA template with the bracketed phasing language and the credit table. If you prefer different bands or caps, tell us and we'll update.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Template_v3.pdf (PDF)

Susan — quick note from the commercial side. We're aligned with Naomi's phasing recommendation. A couple of pragmatic asks from procurement we should flag now so Laura can bake them into the redline:

- Can Cumulus confirm if APAC spend will be billed monthly and separated on invoices? The credit buckets above assume APAC-line-item billing (simpler to credit region-specific outages).
- If you need a lower Phase 1 cap (e.g., 15% instead of 25%) to simplify cost modeling, we can consider that in return for a slightly longer Phase 1 (120 days).

If both of those are acceptable, Laura will propose language that implements the billing-linked crediting and the Phase 1 cap option.

Thanks,
Ben
